chapter: Leaving the band, Strayhorn and reflections
title: Jean Eldridge and the two-bass experiment
summary: Greer recalls the singer on Something to Live For and Duke's use of two basses.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Bass players: lineage, tone and technique

blocks.x: Did you all only use that singer Jean Eldridge, on that one piece, "Something to Live For" or did you all work with her -- you know the one who sings with that little, funny voice? On the first verse of "Something to Live For". Remember, she's got that voice like (humming). She's got that kind of -- you know, the way she had her voice was kind of --
Yeah, she's the one that made that one.
She wasn't with us too long.
Just for that? Oh, I know what I wanted to ask you. How did Ellington strike up on the idea of using two bass players?

I don't know. One of his dreams. He was the first one to do that. How he did it, I do not know. I look around and I see two bass players, good ones. He never had no turkey(?) but they didn't conflict with each other. How he got that idea for using two basses, I never know.
